#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL. A loaded
# machine can take minutes to bring the JVM up; running the specs before it is ready fails every
# one of them for no reason, so wait long and fail loudly rather than run against nothing.
ready=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$ready" != 1 ]; then
  echo "bin/e2e: the app did not become healthy on port ${PORT} within 300s; see .run/app.log" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid

A PENDING claim now stays bound by its person's last statement: it shows and totals the figure the statement bound, like an OPEN claim. On a normal `bin/e2e` run, 3 of the 4 tests pass. "pending bound scenario 1" still fails, and that failure comes from the machine's date, not from this change.

**What changed**
- **Server**: `Claim.isBound()` used to leave out PENDING claims; now it doesn't. Every total, figure and statement that relies on it now treats a bound PENDING claim like any other. I also made approving a PENDING claim settle it at the bound figure, matching how a settle works. No test covers approval, so say if you'd rather it kept using the live figure.
- **Front end**: the `bound()` function in `core/claims.ts` got the same fix, so the screen shows the same figures as the server.
- I updated the comments that described the old rule. Stored data, schema and audit records didn't need to change.

**Test results**
- **Before the change:** "pending bound" and "scenario 1" failed.
- **After the change:** "pending bound", "scenario 2" and "scenario 3" pass. "Scenario 1" still fails at line 322: the current rate for grade C shows `n/a` instead of `5.00`.

**Why scenario 1 still fails:** a new sheet starts with "today" set to the real date (`SheetService.java:92`), and every change is filed under the sheet's today at the time. The test never sets today on the parent sheet, so its rates are recorded under 2026-11-13. When the test then views the child sheet as of 2026-04-02, the parent's rates don't exist yet, and the child's own C rate has ended by then. So the test only passes if the machine clock is on or before 2026-04-02.

To check this, I temporarily made new sheets start on 2026-03-01 and ran `bin/e2e`: **all 4 tests passed**. I then put the line back to `LocalDate.now()`, so that experiment isn't part of the change. I didn't make it permanent because it's unrelated behaviour and the test can't be edited. To get scenario 1 passing, the options are to run on a clock at or before 2026-04-02, or for the test to set a "today" on the parent sheet.
